documents.title: Generative AI Use in Education
documents.stance_why: The page sets no single university rule on student AI use: "Instructors, individually and collectively, may determine whether, when, and how GenAI should be integrated" and each course policy "should state when students must, may, or cannot use GenAI". It gives a fallback ("If an instructor has not explicitly stated that GenAI is allowed for an assignment, assume it isn’t") but that applies only when the instructor is silent, so the document delegates.
documents.summary: University-wide guidelines from the Provost's education subcommittee of the AI Council, with principles plus separate guidance for instructors and students. The decision on whether and how students may use GenAI is left to instructors, who are asked to state per assignment when students must, may or cannot use it; AI is assumed unauthorized when a course is silent. It also covers disclosure, verification, privacy, equity, human oversight of grading, cautious use of detectors, and recommendations on tool approval, literacy training and pilots.
